cases.prompt: The shift-log pilot (fictional) has a business case with two saving rows and a cost estimate of 40 one-time and 10 per year. We want to ask for 100 units for the pilot phase. Please prepare the capital request for the approvers.
cases.expected_output:
The ask is stated in one line: amount, what it buys, which phase, decision date.
The approval route is read from the approval matrix and the approvers are named by role; any ambiguity is flagged for the OD lead rather than guessed.
Tracked and proven value are shown separately and never summed; cost is not netted against value.
Options include a smaller or staged version and do-nothing, and the package closes with open items and one maturity verdict.
The package is a draft for a human to review and submit; nothing is submitted or approved.

cases.prompt: Write the capital request for our new line-monitoring idea. We have not done a cost estimate or a business case yet, but the plant manager wants the request tomorrow.
cases.expected_output:
The assistant applies the refusal gate: value backbone and investment estimate are missing, so it returns de-risk questions instead of a package.
The questions name what is missing and which role supplies it.
It does not invent cost lines or savings.
It points to the value and cost steps that come first.

cases.prompt: We want to reconfigure an existing dashboard that the plant already owns. It costs nothing new and fits the plant roadmap. Do we need a capital request?
cases.expected_output:
The assistant confirms that no capital request is needed when no new money is committed and the work is within the roadmap.
It records that conclusion and stops instead of drafting a package.

cases.prompt: Can you work out how much this use case would save per year so I can put it on the savings list?
cases.expected_output:
The assistant recognises this as value calculation, not a capital request.
It routes to the value-building step (bc-build) and does not draft an eCR.
